description: The control-vector GGUF image written by the Python interp exporter and loaded by the Rust runtime

constraints: N is 1-based: direction.N steers decoder block N, and block 0 is unsteerable
every direction tensor shares one width
at least one direction tensor is present

notes.layer_numbering: direction.N is 1-based because llama.cpp and repeng number control vectors that way, and block 0 is unsteerable. Both sides enforce it independently - export.py refuses min(directions) < 1, and cpu.rs refuses layer < 1 - which is exactly why the end-to-end check matters more than either guard alone. The 0-based counterpart is schemas/probe_artifact.json's 'layer', which names the block whose post-block residual a probe scores; the two artifacts number layers differently on purpose.
notes.reader_ignores: ControlVector::from_gguf reads no metadata at all: it neither checks general.architecture nor uses model_hint or layer_count, and selects tensors purely by the direction. prefix. The two metadata keys are therefore writer-only in practice. Any other GGUF passed as a control vector fails on 'holds no direction.<layer> tensors' rather than on an architecture mismatch.
notes.comparison_is_semantic: The committed fixtures are compared by parsed content - architecture, metadata keys and values, tensor names, widths, and values - never byte for byte. gguf is pinned, but a version bump may legitimately change padding or alignment, and a byte comparison would report that as exporter drift.
notes.float_exactness: Fixture values are chosen to be exact in f32, so a round trip through the writer and the Rust parser is an equality comparison and needs no tolerance.
notes.probe_moved: This contract covered the probe image too until the probe left GGUF for safetensors plus a JSON sidecar. schemas/probe_artifact.json is now its contract. The control vector stays GGUF because llama.cpp reads it as --control-vector-scaled, so the format is not this repository's to choose; the probe had exactly one reader and nothing outside this tree was served by keeping it. runtime/src/gguf.rs exists for this artifact alone now.
